metadata.title: Financial Risk Classification using AI
metadata.note: STEM/AI topic-of-interest video, based on the author's own project: 'Automated Financial Document Risk Classification and Clause Detection.' Reframed around the paper's actual stated objective (per its own Impact Statement): can AI help flag financial risk and catch important legal clauses at a scale manual review can't match, as an assistive decision-support tool, not a replacement for professional judgment. Task 1: Hierarchical BiLSTM on SEC 10-K/10-Q risk classification (95.2% macro-F1, +10.9 over TF-IDF baseline, 116 filings from 15 companies). Task 2: LegalBERT fine-tuned for clause detection on CUAD (80.1% macro-F1 vs 77.6% TF-IDF baseline, using only 5% of training data — with an honest and important limitation: a 43.3% miss rate on present clauses). Built using the same proven pattern set as prior videos: folderLabel set explicitly on ClaudeComposerAsk beats (@HumanitariansAI), OutroCTA used instead of ClaudeTitleOutro, BLUF lines kept short to avoid edge-bleed, no stale sparse_by_design flags except the legitimate BrutalistHesitantWriter typing-beat exemption.
